name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,324

clue.text: Start to regret taking ecstasy after a meal

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of regret
E is the drug ecstasy
past means after, as in half past two

explanation.surface: Someone who took a pill after dinner soon wishes they hadn't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' just strings the first two letters together; 'after' supplies the last four, so 'after a meal' is not one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal or feast.

clue.text: Take great pleasure in continually going over to Luxembourg

indicators.note: going over suggests turning something over, so in a down entry the word is read upward

blocks.note: ever means always, continually
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: Someone keeps travelling to Luxembourg because they enjoy it so much.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel is to take great delight, and 'revel in' is the idiom the surface borrows.

clue.text: Call to mind a bit of advice about crossing Cambodia's principal river

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word for advice is read backwards
something crossing another lies across it, so one piece sits inside the other
the principal letter of a word is its first one

blocks.note: a tip is a piece of advice
the leading letter of Cambodia
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A travel tip about getting over the main river of Cambodia, the Mekong.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed advice goes round the C, then the river is added at the end. The Ure is a Yorkshire river much used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to imagine it, to bring an image of it to mind.

clue.text: Resent failing to receive small backhander

indicators.note: a failing word has broken down, so its letters fall into a new order
receiving something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Someone sulks at missing out on a little bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resent' looks like a verb with a subject missing; it is the letters to rearrange, with the small word slipped in after the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhander is a bribe, and a sweetener is an inducement payment of the same kind.

clue.text: Fail to give a true impression of Frederick at the beginning of Persuasion

indicators.note: the beginning of a name is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.clueFragment: Fail to give a true impression of
blocks.note: to belie is to misrepresent
the opening letter of Frederick

explanation.surface: Captain Frederick Wentworth seems misrepresented at the start of Jane Austen's novel Persuasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Persuasion is an Austen novel whose hero is Frederick Wentworth, which makes it look like a title; here it is the definition, meaning conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuasion is a firmly held opinion or creed, which is what a belief is.

clue.text: Banishment of former priest is overturned

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so in a down entry the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: ex means former
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A retired cleric's sentence of banishment is quashed on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli, the priest who raised Samuel, is crossword shorthand for priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Exile is enforced absence from one's homeland, a synonym for banishment.

clue.text: Minister's first job? To cut Iceland's taxes

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
something that cuts another goes into it, splitting it in two

blocks.note: the opening letter of Minister
a post is a job
IS is the international code for Iceland

explanation.surface: A new finance minister's first act is to cut Icelandic taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposts are duties or levies imposed by a government, which are taxes.

clue.text: Not currently in love like Frank

blocks.note: to fancy someone is to like them
frank and free both mean open and unrestrained in speech

explanation.surface: Someone, like their friend Frank, is unattached at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name and 'like' like a comparison; both are verbs and adjectives in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy-free describes someone not attached romantically, unburdened by any love interest.

clue.text: Put out directive ignoring Irish revolutionary

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so those letters are dropped
a revolution overturns order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
Ir is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: An order is issued that pays no attention to an Irish rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish revolutionary' reads as one figure, but the adjective is removed and the noun signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Evicted means expelled from one's home, put out on the street.

clue.text: A matter for regret admitting pressure on mineworker

indicators.note: admitting something means letting it in, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: a pity is something regrettable
P is the symbol for pressure
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is sad to see so much pressure put on a coal miner.
explanation.walkthrough: Pit ponies were horses that hauled coal underground in British mines, so a 'mineworker' needn't be human.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit pony was a small horse that worked down a coal mine, so it was literally a worker in a mine.

clue.text: Spinoza was one of the first to be seen after blast

indicators.note: this says one piece follows another in the entry rather than going first

blocks.note: to blast a play or film is to pan it, criticise it harshly
taken as written
first is written 1st, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: The philosopher Spinoza appeared early in the aftermath of some explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of the first' looks like a phrase about pioneers; 'of' is the link and 'the first' supplies letters. Blast means criticise, not explode.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinoza identified God with nature, the classic pantheist position, so he is an example of the type.

clue.text: Explain with pictures of the Italian soldiers returning in splendour

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the soldiers are read right to left
the soldiers are put in the word for splendour

blocks.note: il is the Italian for the
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
lustre is brilliance, splendour

explanation.surface: An art book on Italian troops coming home in glory needs plates.
explanation.definitionFit: To illustrate a text is to add pictures that clarify it.

clue.text: Soldiers guarding the earliest of Yankee states

indicators.note: guards surround what they protect, so one piece goes around the other
the earliest letter of a word is its first

blocks.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment
the opening letter of Yankee

explanation.surface: Troops protect the oldest of the American states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankee states' suggests New England; 'states' is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Says and states are both verbs for declaring something in words.

clue.text: Fresh information involving queen from the east

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it inside, so one piece sits within the other
in an across entry, coming from the east means reading from right to left

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: New intelligence about a queen arrives from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means new and unripe or inexperienced, the same sense as fresh.

clue.text: Talk at length about Italian gangster having energy to act without help

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the talking goes round the next pieces

blocks.note: to go on is to talk at length
It is the abbreviation for Italian
Al Capone, the archetypal gangster
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A mobster's long speech about his Italian roots and his independence.
explanation.walkthrough: The talking goes round both Italian and gangster, then energy is tacked on after 'having'.
explanation.definitionFit: To go it alone is the idiom for doing something independently, without assistance.

clue.text: Attempt to capture saint standing by animal in ornamental textile

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so these letters go in
standing by means next to, so one piece is placed beside the other

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
an ape is an animal
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Someone tries to depict a saint beside a beast in a woven hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests St Jerome and his lion woven into a wall-hanging, which fits the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a heavy decorative fabric with woven pictures, an ornamental textile.

clue.text: Fellow salesman standing up to make a speech can be seen in Punch

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing something up means it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
a rep is a sales representative
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: A salesman gets up to make a speech, and it ends up in Punch magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a British humour magazine, so the capital P disguises a verb meaning to pierce.
explanation.definitionFit: To perforate is to make a hole through something, to pierce or punch it.

clue.text: Row over Ms Halliwell's underwear

indicators.note: lying over something means spanning it, so one piece is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: a row is a line
Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice of the Spice Girls

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over a pop star's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Row looks like a quarrel; here it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightclothes.

clue.text: Book showing a form of gneiss seen around Spain

indicators.note: a different form of a word means its letters take a new shape
around means surrounding, so these letters enclose the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written; gneiss is a banded metamorphic rock
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A geology book shows a variety of rock found in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is the first book of the Bible.

clue.text: Take sides with soldier for the most part

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a Ranger is a soldier in a US commando unit

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to back a soldier, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: To range oneself with someone is to align oneself on their side, an old-fashioned idiom for joining a cause.

clue.text: Sniggers as dubiously stricken opponent finally quits

indicators.note: something dubious is unreliable, so these letters are not trusted in their given order
finally points to the last letter of the word before it
a letter that quits leaves, so it is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
the closing letter of opponent

explanation.surface: People snigger when a beaten opponent leaves the field.
explanation.walkthrough: To nicker is to snigger or laugh quietly, an older British word; the plural noun has the same form, which the setter enjoys.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicker is a snigger or suppressed laugh, so the plural verb form matches sniggers.

clue.text: American horse's endless suffering

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a paint is a piebald horse of the American West

explanation.surface: A US horse is in constant agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is physical or mental suffering, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Upset to find candlestick covered with muck

indicators.note: a thing covered with something has it all round, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: muck is dirt
a sconce is a wall bracket holding a candle

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed to discover their candleholder caked in grime.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert is to unsettle or fluster, to upset someone's composure.

clue.text: Act on denial by Republican benefactor

blocks.note: to do is to act
no is a denial
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A wealthy backer responds to a Republican refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods, as a benefactor does.

clue.text: Appropriate for an associate of Cobden to reject hint of bias

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its opening letter
rejecting something means throwing it out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: John Bright campaigned with Richard Cobden against the Corn Laws
the opening letter of bias

explanation.surface: It is proper for a political ally to refuse any suggestion of prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: Cobden and Bright led the Anti-Corn Law League in 1840s Britain, campaigning for free trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and appropriate both mean suitable or proper for the occasion.

clue.text: The intention of Apollo for example revealed by a stroke of luck

blocks.note: Apollo is an example of a god, and 'of Apollo' makes it possessive
an end is an aim or intention

explanation.surface: A lucky break reveals the plan of the god Apollo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apollo for example' stands for a god, and 'of Apollo' makes it possessive; the possessive phrase is then read with the noun after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected welcome event, a piece of good fortune.

clue.text: Try to grasp the point of American board game

indicators.note: the point of something is its tip, so only the leading letter is kept

blocks.note: to have is to hold, grasp
the leading letter of American
Go is the Asian board game of stones

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to understand the purpose of an American board game.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go is the informal idiom for making an attempt.

clue.text: Guarantee heading off reprimand

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and off means it is removed

blocks.note: censure is a formal reprimand

explanation.surface: A promise that heads off a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' looks like preventing; it says the first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain, which is to guarantee an outcome.

clue.text: Son breaks new bidet in rented accommodation

indicators.note: a new version has a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reordered
breaking into something means getting inside, so this letter goes within

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A tenant's son smashes the new bidet in their rented flat.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is a British one-room rented flat, bedroom and sitting room in one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single rented room for living and sleeping, a kind of rented accommodation.
